text: note summarises AED water quality library (libaed-water, coupled GLM) represents sediment nitrogen phosphorus, simulates resuspension. compares two fundamentally different ways parameterising processes gives guidance appropriate multi-decadal climate-scenario runs (e.g. 100-year simulations). statements grounded directly AED source (aed_sedflux.F90, aed_nitrogen.F90, aed_phosphorus.F90, aed_noncohesive.F90, aed_organic_matter.F90) rather documentation, since namelist documentation describe behaviour.

title: GLM-AED: Sediment Nitrogen & Phosphorus Pools and Resuspension
text: Two mechanisms feed nutrients water column sediment: Diffusive/redox exchange (aed_sedflux.F90) — oxygen- temperature-modulated flux rates dissolved NH4, NO3, FRP. either single lake-wide constant, per-benthic-zone constant (&aed_sed_const2d), output full early-diagenesis model (dynamic/dynamic2d, covered detail ). Physical resuspension (aed_noncohesive.F90) — critical-shear-stress erosion law computed , whose mass flux (NCS_resus) reused aed_phosphorus.F90 (adsorbed P) aed_organic_matter.F90 (particulate organic N/P) via fixed stoichiometric ratios, rather module computing erosion physics.

what: The pool does not feed back on the flux
title: GLM-AED: Sediment Nitrogen & Phosphorus Pools and Resuspension
text: critical, non-obvious detail: modules, erosion flux calculation never reads current pool size. Turning mass tracking gives bookkeeping, constraint. erosion parameters chronically outpace deposition, inorganic pool clips hard floor (minimum = zero_) — producing flux discontinuity — organic pools essentially floor (minimum = -1e10, aed_organic_matter.F90:459) can drift deeply negative, physically meaningless territory silently, warning error.

title: GLM-AED: Sediment Nitrogen & Phosphorus Pools and Resuspension
text: special settings required beyond normal resuspension physics — default behaviour simSedimentMass/simSedimentOM left unset. Diffusive fluxes (independent resuspension, always unlimited regardless approach) set directly, e.g.:
code: &aed_noncohesive    num_ss = 1    settling = 1    w_ss = -0.01    rho_ss = 1.6e3    d_ss = 4e-6    resuspension = 1        ! 0=off, 1=static tau_0, 2/3=macrophyte-modified    epsilon = 0.02           ! max erosion rate, g/m2/s    tau_0 = 0.04              ! critical shear stress, N/m2    tau_r = 1.0                ! reference shear stress for normalisation    ! simSedimentMass left unset -> defaults to .false. (unlimited)    sed_porosity = 0.3 /  &aed_phosphorus    ...    simPO4Adsorption = .true.    resuspension = 1    resus_link = 'NCS_resus'   ! reuse the noncohesive erosion flux /  &aed_organic_matter    ...    resuspension = 1    resus_link = 'NCS_resus'    Xsn = 0.005                ! N:sediment mass ratio for resuspended organic N    Xsp = 0.001                ! P:sediment mass ratio for resuspended organic P    ! simSedimentOM left unset -> defaults to 0 (unlimited) / &aed_sedflux    sedflux_model = 'Constant2d' / &aed_sed_const2d    n_zones = 2    active_zones = 1, 2    fsed_amm = 3.4, 0.7    fsed_nit = -0.4, 0.1    fsed_frp = 0.04, 0.06 /

title: GLM-AED: Sediment Nitrogen & Phosphorus Pools and Resuspension
text: Add mass-tracking flags, size initial inventory, expose diagnostics needed monitor :
code: &aed_noncohesive    ! ... same erosion parameters as above, plus:    simSedimentMass = .true.    ss_initial = 0.0           ! water-column initial concentration    sed_porosity = 0.3    diag_level = 5              ! must be > 0 to expose *_sed diagnostics /  &aed_organic_matter    ! ... same resuspension linkage as above, plus:    simSedimentOM = 2           ! 1 = start pools at zero; 2 = initialise from bulk density/%OM    sedimentBulkDens = 1.3e3    ! kg/m3 - use site sediment core data if available    sedimentDepth = 0.5          ! m - the "active" sediment layer depth being tracked    sedimentOMfrac = 0.05        ! fraction of that layer that's organic matter    Xsn = 0.005    Xsp = 0.001 /

title: GLM-AED: Sediment Nitrogen & Phosphorus Pools and Resuspension
text: Default Approach (prescribed/unlimited flux) unless specific research question sediment nutrient stock depletion accumulation . Reasons: matches Fsed_* values conventionally calibrated (observed flux data, implicitly assuming persistent supply), ’s better-validated, standard configuration. carries risk silent, undetected failure mode described — real concern 100-year run early-onset pool depletion partway invalidate back half simulation without error raised. spin-requirement (water-column suspended sediment reaching dynamic equilibrium) short easy verify relative full run length. Use Approach B deliberately, default, research question specifically requires tracking whether sediment nutrient stocks change climate scenario (e.g., “increased storm frequency exhaust erodible sediment P century?”). case, treat mass-balance validation warning box mandatory interpreting results, size initial pool real sediment core data possible, consider reporting depletion trajectory result rather nuisance spun away. middle-ground option worth considering: run Approach primary configuration (robustness), also enable Approach B diagnostics (simSedimentMass = .true., diag_level > 0) purely monitoring overlay — .e., let flux behave unlimited, still track implied cumulative depletion , treat point tracked figure go negative flag resuspension behaving unrealistically period scenario.

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: General Lake Model (GLM) one-dimensional (1-D), variable-layer hydrodynamic model lakes, reservoirs, estuaries. Originally described Hipsey et al. (2019), GLM simulates vertical profiles temperature, salinity, density driven surface heat exchange, shortwave radiation, wind mixing, inflows, outflows. key architectural features include: Variable-thickness layer scheme — layers merge split dynamically, giving high resolution needed (near thermocline) coarser resolution elsewhere. Flexible inflow/outflow — supports multiple rivers, surface spillways, subsurface outlets arbitrary elevations. Rich surface heat-flux options — sensible heat, latent heat, longwave, shortwave radiation computed standard meteorological inputs. Sediment heat exchange — allows depth-varying bed temperatures drive conductive heat flux water column. detailed GLM documentation available GLM website, Source code: :github: https://github.com/AquaticEcoDynamics/GLM/tree/master Binaries: :github: https://github.com/AquaticEcoDynamics/Binaries

Setting use_bgc = TRUE writes aed/aed.nml file supporting CSV parameter files phytoplankton, zooplankton, macrophytes. configuration files stored configuration slot aeme object. title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: AED modules independent one another — reference state variables computed another module switched . example, aed_nitrogen reduces ammonium using OXY_oxy oxidant, requires aed_oxygen also active; , GLM aborts runtime “Undefined variable” error rather silently ignoring missing link. build_aeme() resolves automatically: set simulate = TRUE biogeochemical variable via model_controls, initialise_aed() determines module variable belongs , walks dependency graph fixed point, adding every module dependency chain requires — never need enable module’s prerequisites hand. one place isn’t automatic set_glm_aed_models() (used ), sets active-module list exactly given, include full chain call directly. (aed_options(modules = ) adds prerequisites unless set resolve_deps = FALSE.) dependency graph, verified directly target-variable links configured AEME’s bundled aed.nml template: AED module dependency requirements enforced initialise_aed(). example, requesting NIT_tn (total nitrogen) model_controls looks like single-variable request, diagnostic total computed aed_totals, aed_totals turn depends nitrogen, phosphorus, organic matter, phytoplankton, build_aeme() activates following module set automatically:
code: aed_sedflux   └─ aed_oxygen           (sediment oxygen demand)        ├─ aed_silica          (silica reactant = OXY_oxy)        ├─ aed_nitrogen        (nitrification reactant = OXY_oxy; also needs aed_sedflux directly)        ├─ aed_phosphorus      (P release reactant = OXY_oxy; also needs aed_sedflux directly)        └─ aed_organic_matter  (mineralisation reactant = OXY_oxy)             ├─ needs aed_nitrogen        (DON mineralisation product)             ├─ needs aed_phosphorus      (DOP mineralisation product = PHS_frp)             ├─ aed_zooplankton      (excretion/mortality targets)             └─ aed_phytoplankton    (uptake/excretion/mortality targets;                                       needs aed_oxygen, aed_nitrogen,                                       aed_phosphorus, aed_silica, and                                       aed_organic_matter directly)                  └─ aed_totals      (TN/TP/TOC totals aggregate state                                       variables owned by aed_nitrogen,                                       aed_phosphorus, aed_organic_matter,                                       and aed_phytoplankton)  aed_macrophyte  (no enforced dependencies — no target-variable links in the                  bundled template) mc <- get_model_controls(use_bgc = TRUE) |>   set_vars_sim(vars_sim = "NIT_tn")  aeme_nit_tn <- build_aeme(   aeme           = aeme,   model          = model,   path           = path,   model_controls = mc,   ext_elev       = 5,   use_bgc        = TRUE )  config_files <- get_model_config_files(aeme)   nml <- read_nml(config_files$glm_aed["aed"]) get_nml_value(nml, "models") #> [1] "aed_sedflux"        "aed_noncohesive"    "aed_oxygen"         #> [4] "aed_silica"         "aed_nitrogen"       "aed_phosphorus"     #> [7] "aed_organic_matter" "aed_phytoplankton"  "aed_totals"

title: GLM-AED: The General Lake Model coupled with AED
text: One important GLM-AED features water-quality simulation depth-varying sediment parameters. GLM divides lake bed sediment zones, temperature regime (using aed_sedflux Constant2d mode) sediment–water interface fluxes oxygen nutrients. Deeper zones typically accumulate organic matter, experience longer periods anoxia, therefore higher sediment oxygen demand (SOD) nutrient release shallow littoral zones.

text: vignette demonstrated key GLM-AED-specific features available AEME: Model description — GLM provides variable-layer 1-D hydrodynamics; AED supplies modular biogeochemistry ranging simple oxygen dynamics full nutrient–phytoplankton food-web simulation. Module selection — set_glm_aed_models() lets enable disable individual AED modules match complexity data requirements application. Sediment zones — estimate_sed_zones() → glm_sed_params() → set_aed_sed_const2d() workflow automatically derives depth-varying sediment parameters lake hypsograph optional near-bed observations. Configuration visualisation — plot_glm_config() provides interactive overview model setup. Diagnostics — run_glm_aed_diagnostics() plot_glm_diagnostics() offer structured, automated checks common biogeochemical issues (unrealistic concentrations, oxygen anomalies, excessive negligible fluxes). Parameter access — get_aeme_parameters() makes easy explore modify individual model parameters manual tuning automated calibration (see aemetools package).

title: Hourly vs daily meteorological forcing
text: AEME accepts meteorological forcing regular time step. two common choices daily (one row per day, historical default) hourly (sub-daily, e.g. ERA5 native resolution). article explains changes switch daily hourly forcing, — importantly — change expressed differently three hydrodynamic models (GLM-AED, GOTM-WET, Simstrat-AED2). single important thing understand: AEME never temporally disaggregates forcing. invent sub-daily structure daily inputs. Sub-daily output therefore requires sub-daily input. daily-vs-hourly changes () much real sub-daily variability model sees, (b) model fills gaps timestamps supplied. temporally disaggregate forcing, use metscale package, can generate sub-daily forcing daily inputs. second point easy miss: meteorological time step model integration time step. Even “daily” AEME run integrates internally time(aeme)$time_step (3600 s default) GLM GOTM, 300 s Simstrat. Daily forcing make physics daily — makes forcing daily.

title: Hourly vs daily meteorological forcing
text: AEME defines MET_pprain MET_ppsnow rate mm/day. Every model met-writer assumes — make_met_glm() divides 1000 get m/day, make_met_simstrat() 1000 * 24 get m/hr, make_met_gotm() 86400. Sub-daily reanalysis products (ERA5 tp, AWS logs) instead report precipitation accumulation per timestep — millimetres fell hour. Numerically two identical daily data (mm day = mm/day, daily path always “just worked”); identical sub-daily, accumulation 0.4 mm hour rate 9.6 mm/day. standardise_met() now resolves automatically: meteo sub-daily rescales MET_pprain / MET_ppsnow per-step accumulation mm/day rate 86400 / step_seconds, says : build_aeme() calls standardise_met() , nothing extra needed. sub-daily precipitation genuinely already mm/day rate, opt standardise_met(met, precip_accum = FALSE). check shows effect — sum raw hourly values day (≈ true daily total) lines daily file, mean ~1/24 ; automatic x24 rescale turns per-hour values daily-total rate:
code: i Sub-daily meteo: rescaled "MET_pprain" and "MET_ppsnow" from a per-3600-s   accumulation to a mm/day rate (x24). library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)  hourly_met <- readr::read_csv(   system.file("extdata/lake/data/meteo_era5_hr.csv.gz", package = "AEME"),   show_col_types = FALSE ) |>   mutate(Date = as.POSIXct(Date, tz = "UTC"))  daily_met <- collapse_met_daily(hourly_met, precip = "sum")  hourly_daily <- hourly_met |>   mutate(day = as.Date(Date)) |>   group_by(day) |>   summarise(rain_sum  = sum(MET_pprain),   # ≈ true daily total (mm)             rain_mean = mean(MET_pprain),  # per-hour mean (mm/hr)             .groups = "drop")  daily_met |>   transmute(day = Date, rain_daily = MET_pprain) |>   inner_join(hourly_daily, by = "day") |>   summarise(     mean_daily_source     = mean(rain_daily),     mean_hourly_summed     = mean(rain_sum),     mean_hourly_permin      = mean(rain_mean),     ratio_summed_to_daily   = mean(rain_sum)  / mean(rain_daily),     ratio_permin_to_daily   = mean(rain_mean) / mean(rain_daily)   ) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   mean_daily_source mean_hourly_summed mean_hourly_permin ratio_summed_to_daily #>               <dbl>              <dbl>              <dbl>                 <dbl> #> 1              3.34               3.34              0.139                     1 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: ratio_permin_to_daily <dbl>

code: library(AEME) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr)  aeme   <- readRDS(system.file("extdata/aeme.rds", package = "AEME")) models <- models_ready  # the default controls already derive HYD_strat / HYD_thmcln; add the two # extra stratification diagnostics this article uses mc <- get_model_controls() |>   set_vars_sim(c("HYD_schstb", "HYD_epidep"), simulate = TRUE)  hourly_met <- readr::read_csv(   system.file("extdata/lake/data/meteo_era5_hr.csv.gz", package = "AEME"),   show_col_types = FALSE )  # daily forcing = the SAME data at a daily step. collapse_met_daily() averages # every variable over the day; precip = "sum" because the raw ERA5 file reports # rain/snow as a per-hour accumulation, not a mm/day rate. daily_met <- collapse_met_daily(hourly_met, precip = "sum")  # With its shipped parameters Simstrat keeps this small, hill-sheltered lake # essentially unstratified, which leaves nothing for the daily-vs-hourly switch # to act on. Two hydrodynamic parameters are nudged so it stratifies like the # other two models (see "Making Simstrat stratify", below): #   a_seiche  0.0042 -> 0.001   less wind energy into the internal seiche #   f_wind    1.22   -> 0.8     scale down the (over-exposed) reanalysis wind simstrat_tuning <- list(`ModelParameters.a_seiche` = 0.001,                         `ModelParameters.f_wind`   = 0.8)  run_one <- function(met, tag) {   path <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("hrdaily_", tag))   a <- aeme |>     add_met(met = met) |>     set_time(start = "2020-08-01 00:00:00", stop = "2022-07-31 00:00:00",              spin_up = 35) |>     set_output_time_step("3 hours") |>     build_aeme(path = path, model = models, model_controls = mc, ext_elev = 5)    if ("simstrat_aed2" %in% models) {     do.call(set_simstrat_param, c(       list(file.path(get_lake_dir(a, path), "simstrat_aed2")), simstrat_tuning     ))   }   run_aeme(a, model = models, path = path, model_controls = mc, verbose = FALSE) }  runs <- list(daily = run_one(daily_met, "daily"),              hourly = run_one(hourly_met, "hourly"))  # helper: pull one variable from both runs, for one or more models, into a # long data frame grab <- function(v, mods = models, ...) {   bind_rows(lapply(names(runs), function(tag) {     bind_rows(lapply(mods, function(m) {       d <- tryCatch(         get_var(runs[[tag]], model = m, var_sim = v, remove_spin_up = TRUE, ...),         error = function(e) NULL       )       if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d)) return(NULL)       transmute(d, Date, value, var = v, model = m, forcing = tag)     }))   })) }

Given enough lead-, physics forgets initial guess – surface heat exchange, mixing inflow/outflow replace guessed state one consistent forcing. much lead-“enough” depends variable: surface mixed layer re-equilibrates atmosphere days; hypolimnion ventilated lake mixes, wrong deep temperature can survive stratified season; biogeochemical pools turn timescale sources sinks – weeks years. short spin-leaves initial-condition bias results easy mistake model error. long spin-wastes forcing data compute, AEME run : check_time() requires meteorological (inflow) forcing span start - spin_up stop. article shows set initial state AEME 0.4.0 functions, treat initial guess one axis ensemble uncertainty, use assess_spin_up() choose spin-length long enough longer. use example lake shipped package. title: Introduction to AEME
text: AEME package hosts four one-dimensional hydrodynamic models: DYnamic REservoir Simulation Model (DYRESM), General Lake Model (GLM), General Ocean Turbulence Model (GOTM, adapted closed basins application lakes reservoirs), Simstrat. models can coupled corresponding water quality models, DYRESM-CAEDYM (Computational Aquatic Ecosystem Dynamics Model), GLM-AED (Aquatic Ecosystem Dynamics Model), GOTM-WET (Water Ecosystem Tool), Simstrat-AED2/AED. vignette assumes least one model already installed – see vignette("installing-models") build_aeme() reports missing executable. Key aspects AEME package include: Defined S4 class aeme objects Configuration models common standardised inputs Standardised calibration, manipulation visualisation

title: Introduction to AEME
text: aeme object main object AEME package. S4 class contains information required run model. aeme object contains following slots: lake - list object containing information lake (name, id, latitude, longitude, elevation, depth, area) time - list object containing information time (start, stop, spin_up, time_step) configuration - list object containing information configuration (model_controls, dy_cd, glm_aed, gotm_wet) observations - list object containing information observations (lake, level) inputs - list object containing information inputs (init_profile, init_depth, hypsograph, meteo, use_lw, Kw) inflows - list object containing information inflows (data, factor) outflows - list object containing information outflows (data, outflow_lvl, factor) water_balance - list object containing information water balance configuration (use, method, data) parameters - data.frame describing parameters input column names (model, file, name, value, min, max, module, group) output - list object containing information outputs (n_members)

title: Introduction to AEME
text: lake slot contains information lake. list object contains following objects: name - Name lake (character). id - Lake ID (character numeric). latitude - Latitude lake (numeric). provided, latitude calculated centroid shape. longitude - Longitude lake (numeric). provided, longitude calculated centroid shape. elevation - Elevation lake (numeric). shape - Shape lake (sf object). shape lake can represented polygon. centroid polygon used calculate latitude longitude lake. depth - Max depth lake (m) (numeric). Depth area used generate simple hypsographic curve none provided inputs slot. area - Surface area lake (m2) (numeric) Objects bold required building running model.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: time slot contains information time. list object contains following objects: start - Start date simulation (character). start date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. stop - End date simulation (character). end date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. timestep - Timestep simulation (numeric). timestep must seconds. spin_up - List spin periods simulation model (numeric). spin period must days. spin period period time model run simulation period. spin period used initialise model discarded examining simulation period.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: configuration slot list contains model configurations. includes configurations files hydrodynamic components well aquatic ecosystem model components: Files hydrodynamic ecosystem models. build_aeme() ran, model_controls data.frame passed function argument added configuration slot. details model_controls, see ’s section .

title: Introduction to AEME
text: observations slot list contains observations -lake (lake) variables (e.g. water temperature, chlorophyll-, dissolved oxygen etc.) water level (level). observations used assess model performance using function also calibrate model using aemetools package. lake observations stored data frame following required columns: Date - Date observation (character). date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. depth - Nominal sampling depth observation (m, numeric), positive-lake surface. var_aeme - Variable name observation (character). variable names input preparation described AEME inputs article. value - Value observation (numeric). Two optional columns also recognised: depth_to (bottom integrated sample, observation covers depth interval) sd (measurement standard deviation, variable’s units, used observation weighting calibration). legacy depth_from / depth_to column pair still accepted collapsed single depth (interval midpoint) deprecation warning. level observations stored data frame following columns: Date - Date observation (character). date must format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. value - Value observation (numeric). value must metres sea level within range hypsograph elevations.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: input slot list contains following objects: init_profile - profile initialise lake simulation (data.frame). columns: “depth”, “temperature” “salt”. provided, automatically generated using values model_controls. init_depth - depth lake initialising model (vector), provided, assume depth hypsograph. hypsograph - lake hypsograph. data.frame columns “elev”, “depth” “area”. data, can generate one using generate_hypsograph() function. meteo - meteorological data. data.frame minimum must contain columns date (“Date”), air temperature (“MET_tmpair), wind speed (”MET_wndspd”) shortwave radiation (“MET_radswd”). See AEME Inputs use_lw - Logical switch use longwave radiation. Defaults TRUE. Kw - light extinction coefficient (m−1m^{-1}).

title: Introduction to AEME
text: inflows slot list contains following objects: data - named list data.frames contain columns date (“Date”), flow (“HYD_flow”; m3day−1m^3 day^{-1}). Temperature can also provided (“HYD_temp”), however provided estimated using air temperature. name list used stream identifier model. method water_balance section set to3, “wbal” added data, contains separate inflow model, estimated using different evaporation functions inside model. factor - list scaling factors applied inflows. Named according model. inflows present slot empty.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: outflows slot list contains following objects: data - named list data.frames contain columns date (“Date”), flow (“HYD_flow”; m3day−1m^3 day^{-1}). method water_balance section set 2 3, “wbal” added data, contains separate outflow model, estimated using different evaporation functions inside model. factor - list scaling factors applied outflows. Named according model. However, can also passed parameter model_parameters section calibrated . preferred method applying scaling factors. elevation - named list elevations outflows occur. important falls within elevation range hypsograph. Set -1 outflow surface. outflows present slot empty.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: water balance slot generated internally build_aeme() function called wb_method set 2 3. slot contains: use: define lake level use. Can either observed (“obs”) modelled (“mod”) lake level. Default = “obs”. method: can 1 (inflows outflows) 2 (outflows calculated) 3 (inflows outflows calculated). default 2 . data: list two data.frames. “wbal” contains diagnostics estimating evaporation water balance model “model” contains modelled lake water level use “mod”.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: parameters slot contains data.frame parameters used building model. update default model parameters scale meteorological scale inflows outflows model. columns parameters data.frame : model - Either “dy_cd”, “glm_aed” “gotm_wet”. file - Either name file e.g. “glm3.nml” model specific files (whichever glm3.nml/glm4.nml actually disk resolved automatically – see find_glm_nml() – table entry always uses literal string "glm3.nml" regardless GLM version object built ) “met” meteorological variables “inf” inflow “wdr” outflows. (Outflows initiallly referred withdrawals, hence “wdr” notation, probably updated reflect current outflows slot soon…). name - Name parameter. name parameter nested nml/yaml file, whole hierarchy needs provide level separated “/” e.g. “light/Kw” Kw GLM-AED. value - Value parameter. min - Minimum range parameter. used aemetools::calib_aeme() aemetools::sa_aeme() function. max - Maximum range parameter. used aemetools::calib_aeme() aemetools::sa_aeme() function. group - Phytoplankton group. used GOTM-WET phytoplankton parameters. index - Index parameter. used GLM-AED parameters vectors e.g. sediment parameters (“sed_temp_mean”). module - Module parameter . necessary, helpful identifying parameters module GLM-AED GOTM-WET. function get_aeme_parameters() allows select parameters based model module. See ?get_aeme_parameters() details.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: output slot list updated run_aeme() executed. time executed, variable outputs designated model_controls added Aeme object.

title: Introduction to AEME
text: model_controls data.frame generated get_model_controls(). data.frame columns: var_aeme - character; AEME variable name simulate - logical; add variable Aeme object inf_default - numeric; default value use inflows none present inflows. particularly important configuring water chemistry inflows use_bgc = TRUE. initial_wc - numeric; value use initialising model. automatically updated variable present observations slot. initial_sed - numeric; value use initialising sediment module DYRESM-CAEDYM model. conversion_aed - numeric; factor multiply convert GLM-AED units. model built, model_controls data.frame stored configuration slot aeme object. can retrieved get_model_controls(aeme = aeme).

title: Introduction to AEME
text: aeme object can created using aeme_constructor() function. requires minimum lake, time, input list objects. object can also created YAML file using yaml_to_aeme() function. YAML file contains information required run model.
code: # Define lake list lat <- -36.88921 lon <- 174.4669 depth <- 13.08 area <- 153648  lake <- list(     latitude = lat,     longitude = lon,     # elevation = elevation,     depth = depth,     area = area   ) time <- list(   start = as.POSIXct("2020-07-01"),   stop = as.POSIXct("2022-06-30") )  hypsograph <- generate_hypsograph(max_depth = depth, surface_area = area,                                   volume_development = 1.2)  met <- aemetools::get_era5_land_point_nz(lat = lat, lon = lon,                                          years = 2020:2022)  #' Define input list input = list(   hypsograph = hypsograph,   meteo = met,   Kw = 1.21 )  aeme <- aeme_constructor(lake = lake, time = time, input = input) slotNames(aeme) #>  [1] "lake"          "time"          "configuration" "observations"  #>  [5] "input"         "inflows"       "outflows"      "water_balance" #>  [9] "output"        "parameters"

code: inp <- input(aeme) names(inp) #> [1] "init_profile" "init_depth"   "hypsograph"   "meteo"        "use_lw"       #> [6] "Kw"

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: Reservoirs differ natural lakes several ways important hydrodynamic modelling: Regulated water levels – reservoir levels managed controlled releases rather natural outlet seepage. surface spillway activates reservoir near full capacity. penstock bottom outlet daily operational releases. mid-level selective withdrawal outlet water quality management (e.g. avoid releasing cold, anoxic hypolimnetic water). Thermal stratification management – withdrawals different depth layers affect downstream temperature water quality. AEME supports three major 1-D hydrodynamic models (DYRESM-CAEDYM, GLM-AED, GOTM-WET) multiple outlets arbitrary elevations. vignette walks setting reservoir ensemble model two outlets different levels: regulated penstock depth surface spillway.

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
code: library(AEME) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr)

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: use fictional reservoir, Reservoir, located North Island New Zealand. reservoir full supply level 150 m sea level maximum depth 25 m.
code: lat   <- -37.80 lon   <- 176.00 elev  <- 150   # full supply level (m a.s.l.) depth <- 25    # maximum depth (m) area  <- 1.2e6 # surface area at full supply level (m²)  reservoir <- list(   name      = "Reservoir",   id        = "res001",   latitude  = lat,   longitude = lon,   elevation = elev,   depth     = depth,   area      = area )

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: Meteorological data bundled AEME package (originally Lake Wainamu, North Island) reused drive reservoir simulation.

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: hypsograph describes relationship elevation surface area (thus volume). Constructed reservoirs typically prismatic (box-like) shape compared natural lakes. reflected higher volume_development parameter (values > 1.5 give convex, cylindrical shape; value 3 corresponds perfect cylinder).
code: hypsograph <- generate_hypsograph(   max_depth          = depth,   surface_area       = area,   volume_development = 2.5,   # more prismatic than a natural lake   elev               = elev,   ext_elev           = 2      # extend 2 m above full supply level )  head(hypsograph) #>    elev depth    area #> 1 152.0   2.0 1391324 #> 2 150.0   0.0 1200000 #> 3 149.8  -0.2 1176144 #> 4 149.6  -0.4 1152574 #> 5 149.4  -0.6 1129291 #> 6 149.2  -0.8 1106292 ggplot(hypsograph, aes(x = area / 1e6, y = elev)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#0065a9") +   geom_point(size = 1.5, colour = "#0065a9") +   labs(     x     = expression("Area (km"^2 * ")"),     y     = "Elevation (m a.s.l.)",     title = "Reservoir – hypsograph"   ) +   theme_bw()

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: create synthetic seasonal inflow time series typical New Zealand catchment, higher flows winter (June–August) lower flows summer. inflow data frame must contain minimum Date HYD_flow (m³ day⁻¹). Temperature (HYD_temp, °C) salinity (CHM_salt, PSU) columns recommended.
code: set.seed(42) sim_dates <- seq(as.Date("2020-01-01"), as.Date("2021-12-31"), by = "day") doy       <- as.integer(format(sim_dates, "%j"))  # Seasonal signal: peak winter flow ~day 200 (NZ Southern Hemisphere winter) inflow_flow <- pmax(5000,   80000 + 60000 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 200) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 8000))  # River temperature: coolest in winter, warmest in summer inflow_temp <- pmax(4, 15 - 8 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 15) / 365))  inflow_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = inflow_flow,   HYD_temp = inflow_temp,   CHM_salt = 0 )  head(inflow_data[, 1:3]) #>         Date HYD_flow HYD_temp #> 1 2020-01-01 33371.71 7.231200 #> 2 2020-01-02 17605.56 7.199484 #> 3 2020-01-03 24764.44 7.170079 #> 4 2020-01-04 26675.80 7.142995 #> 5 2020-01-05 24617.84 7.118239 #> 6 2020-01-06 20322.85 7.095819

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: key feature demonstrated vignette configuration two outlets different elevations: Visualise inflow outflows simulation period:  penstock provides near-constant regulated release throughout year, spillway flows high-flow winter months.
code: # Penstock: regulated base flow with small seasonal variation penstock_flow <- pmax(0,   60000 + 15000 * sin(2 * pi * (doy - 100) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 4000))  # Spillway: only active during the high-inflow winter period spillway_flow <- pmax(0,   25000 * cos(2 * pi * (doy - 200) / 365) +     rnorm(length(sim_dates), mean = 0, sd = 5000))  penstock_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = penstock_flow )  spillway_data <- data.frame(   Date     = sim_dates,   HYD_flow = spillway_flow ) flows <- bind_rows(   mutate(inflow_data[, c("Date", "HYD_flow")], stream = "Inflow"),   mutate(penstock_data, stream = "Penstock (130 m)"),   mutate(spillway_data, stream = "Spillway (surface)") ) |>   filter(Date >= as.Date("2020-08-01"),          Date <= as.Date("2021-06-30"))  ggplot(flows, aes(x = Date, y = HYD_flow / 1e3, colour = stream)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c("Inflow"             = "#0065a9",                "Penstock (130 m)"   = "#d73027",                "Spillway (surface)" = "#4dac26"),     name = NULL   ) +   labs(     x     = "Date",     y     = expression("Flow (×10"^3 * " m"^3 * " day"^{-1} * ")"),     title = "Simulated inflow and outflow discharges"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: important subsurface outlet elevation falls within elevation range hypsograph. illustrate two outlets sit relative reservoir hypsograph.
code: outlet_lines <- data.frame(   elev  = c(130, max(hypsograph$elev)),   label = c("Penstock (130 m)", "Spillway (surface)") )  ggplot(hypsograph, aes(x = area / 1e6, y = elev)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(xmin = 0, xmax = area / 1e6), fill = "#cce5f7", alpha = 0.6) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#0065a9") +   geom_hline(data = outlet_lines,              aes(yintercept = elev, colour = label),              linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.9) +   scale_colour_manual(     values = c("Penstock (130 m)"   = "#d73027",                "Spillway (surface)" = "#4dac26"),     name = "Outlet"   ) +   labs(     x     = expression("Area (km"^2 * ")"),     y     = "Elevation (m a.s.l.)",     title = "Outlet positions on reservoir hypsograph"   ) +   theme_bw() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Reservoir Simulation with Multiple Outlets
text: vignette shown configure AEME reservoir multiple outlets different elevations. key steps : Define reservoir geometry using prismatic hypsograph (volume_development > 1.5) appropriate constructed reservoir. Create time series inflow outlet independently. Register multiple outlets add_outflows(), providing named data list matching named elevation list. Use elevation = -1 surface outlet; provide actual elevation (m .s.l.) subsurface outlets, ensuring values fall within hypsograph elevation range. Build run model ensemble build_aeme() run_aeme(). Currently one three hydrodynamic models, GLM-AED, supported AEME (DYRESM-CAEDYM, GLM-AED, GOTM-WET) can handle multiple outlets produce separate outlet files build step, allowing outlet’s contribution tracked independently.

code: hyps <- get_hypsograph(aeme)  orig_hyps <- hyps |> dplyr::filter(depth <= 0)  ggplot(orig_hyps, aes(x = area, y = depth)) +   geom_line(colour = "#0065a9", linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = "Area (m²)", y = "Depth (m)",        title = "Original Hypsograph for Lake Rotoehu") +   theme_bw() # Lake Rotoehy lake id is 40188 shoreline <- aemetools::get_lake_shape(id = 40188) # lake shoreline shapefile  # Get lake depth contours contours  <- ltapi::lt_fetch(   "lake_contours",   filter = ltapi::lt_filter(lernzmp_id == "LID40188") ) |>   dplyr::mutate(depth = depth_m) tm_shape(contours) +   tm_lines(col = "depth", scale = tm_scale("-brewer.blues")) +   tm_shape(shoreline) +   tm_borders(col = "black") +   tm_title("Lake Rotoehu Depth Contours") bathy_raster <- rasterise_bathy(shoreline = shoreline,                                 contours  = contours,                                 res = 8, crs = 2193) #> No islands found. #> ℹ Generating depth points for interpolation #> Warning: large number of points for interpolation (95645) #> ✔ Generating depth points for interpolation [5.6s] #>  #> ℹ Interpolating depth points to raster #> ℹ Adjusting depths >= 0 to -0.4m #> ℹ Interpolating depth points to raster #> ✔ Interpolating depth points to raster [1.1s] lake_elev <- max(contours$elevation_m) upd_hyps  <- bathy_to_hypso(bathy_raster) |>   dplyr::mutate(elev = lake_elev + depth) |>    extrap_hyps(z_range = 0.05, ext_elev = 3)  ggplot(orig_hyps, aes(x = area, y = depth)) +   geom_line(colour = "#0065a9", linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_line(data = upd_hyps, aes(x = area, y = depth),             colour = "#d73027", linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = "Area (m²)", y = "Depth (m)",        title = "Hypsograph for Lake Rotoehu",        subtitle = "Blue = original; Red = updated from bathymetric contours") +   theme_bw() aeme <- add_hypsograph(aeme, hypsograph = upd_hyps)

text: measured surface temperatures (HYD_temp) present lake observations, predicted temperature observed timestep nudged toward observation using relaxation scheme: Ts(t+1)=Tspred+Δtτrelax(Tsobs−Tspred)T_s(t+1) = T_s^{pred} + \frac{\Delta t}{\tau_{relax}}\left(T_s^{obs} - T_s^{pred}\right) behaviour depends observation frequency: Frequent observations (weekly better): simulated surface temperature closely tracks lake. text: saturation vapour pressure water surface computed Magnus formula: es(Ts)=exp⁡(2.3026×(7.5TsTs+237.3+0.7858))[hPa]e_s(T_s) = \exp\!\left(2.3026 \times \left(\frac{7.5\,T_s}{T_s + 237.3} + 0.7858\right)\right) \quad \text{[hPa]} exponential increase temperature warm lakes evaporate substantially cold ones even wind speed.
code: Ts_vals <- seq(0, 30, by = 5) es_vals <- sat_vapour_pressure(Ts_vals) data.frame(Ts_degC = Ts_vals, es_hPa = round(es_vals, 2)) #>   Ts_degC es_hPa #> 1       0   6.11 #> 2       5   8.72 #> 3      10  12.28 #> 4      15  17.05 #> 5      20  23.38 #> 6      25  31.67 #> 7      30  42.42

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: latent heat flux (W/m²) computed using bulk aerodynamic formula. evaporative heat loss retained (result capped zero condensation add water lake): Qlh=min⁡(0.622PCeρairLvU(ea−es),0)Q_{lh} = \min\!\left(\frac{0.622}{P}\,C_e\,\rho_{air}\,L_v\,U\,(e_a - e_s),\ 0\right) vapour pressure deficit (ea−es)(e_a - e_s) drives evaporation. warm surface raises ese_s, increasing deficit evaporative flux. High winds increase turbulent moisture transport.
code: # Example: 20 °C lake, 15 °C air, ~60 % relative humidity, 3 m/s wind Ts <- 20;  Ta <- 15;  U <- 3 ea <- 0.60 * sat_vapour_pressure(Ta)   # ~60 % RH Qlh <- latent_heat_flux(Ts = Ts, wndspd = U, prvapr = ea) cat(sprintf("Latent heat flux: %.1f W/m²\n", Qlh)) #> Latent heat flux: -93.1 W/m²

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: heat flux converted evaporation rate metres per day: E=QlhLvρw×86400[m/day]E = \frac{Q_{lh}}{L_v\,\rho_w} \times 86400 \quad \text{[m/day]}
code: E_m_day <- flux_to_evap(Qlh) cat(sprintf("Evaporation rate: %.4f m/day  (%.1f mm/day)\n",             E_m_day, E_m_day * 1000)) #> Evaporation rate: -0.0033 m/day  (-3.3 mm/day)

title: Lake Rotoehu Water Balance and Evaporation
text: article demonstrated : Load refine lake data Lake Rotoehu using aemetools bathytools. Choose water balance method: Method 1 (closed lake): meteorology ; estimates evaporation residual precipitation volume change. Method 2 (fitted outflow): optimises weir-type rating curve (Ot=C⋅(ht−hinv)1.5O_t = C \cdot (h_t - h_{inv})^{1.5}) observed water levels; preferred method gauge record available. Method 3 (inflow + outflow residual): partitions unexplained storage changes effective inflows spill outflows; useful gauged inflows known budget still close. Understand surface temperature estimation: energy-balance model integrates forward time nudged toward observations via relaxation scheme (default τ=3days\tau = 3\,\text{days}). Without observations linear air-temperature regression seeds initial condition. Trace evaporation calculation three exported functions — sat_vapour_pressure(), latent_heat_flux(), flux_to_evap() — corresponding step bulk aerodynamic method. Visualise summarise evaporation using plot_output() (variable "LKE_evprte"), plot_est_wbal(), plot_wbal(), get_var().

title: Set up AEME for a new lake
text: hypsograph data lake, can use input model. critical input model, defines relationship lake area lake elevation. However, hypsograph data, model use simple cone-shaped hypsograph based lake depth area. ideal, work example. Required column names hypsograph data area, elev, depth.  can see, hypsograph simple cone shape. Ideally, detailed hypsograph data lake. information regarding maximum depth lake, surface area estimate volume development, can generate hypsograph using generate_hypsograph function. volume_development parameter scaling factor volume development lake. Values 1.5 lakes concave hypsograph, values 1.5 lakes convex hypsograph, values 1.5 lakes linear hypsograph. Wainamu Lake, use volume development 1.62 calculated bathymetry survey lake. can view LERNZmp platform.
code: # Generate a simple hypsograph hypsograph_simple <- data.frame(area = c(area, 0),                           elev = c(elevation, elevation - depth),                          depth = c(0, -depth)) hypsograph_simple #>       area  elev  depth #> 1 151938.6 29.00   0.00 #> 2      0.0 15.93 -13.07 # Plot the hypsograph library(ggplot2)  ggplot(hypsograph_simple, aes(x = area, y = elev)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   xlab("Area (m2)") +   ylab("Elevation (m)") +   theme_bw() # Generate a hypsograph hypsograph <- generate_hypsograph(max_depth = depth, surface_area = area,                                   volume_development = 0.5, elev = elevation,                                   ext_elev = 1)  ggplot(hypsograph, aes(x = area, y = elev)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   geom_line(data = hypsograph_simple, aes(x = area, y = elev),              linetype = "dashed") +   xlab("Area (m2)") +   ylab("Elevation (m)") +   theme_bw() # Define input list input <- list(     init_depth = depth,     hypsograph = hypsograph,     meteo = met,     use_lw = TRUE,     Kw = Kw   )

title: Simstrat-AED2: The 1-D k-epsilon lake model coupled with AED2
text: Simstrat one-dimensional (1-D), k-epsilon lake model physical simulation stratification mixing water reservoirs, including basin morphology, atmospheric interaction, inflow/outflow. reservoir represented horizontally-averaged, vertically-resolved water column whose evolution driven atmospheric forcing. Simstrat originally described Goudsmit et al. (2002) since applied lakes reservoirs wide range physical properties. key architectural features include: k-epsilon turbulence closure — turbulent kinetic energy (k) dissipation rate (epsilon) explicitly modelled, alongside water velocities, temperature, salinity, buoyancy. Internal seiche parameterisation — fraction wind energy converted seiche (internal wave) energy, redistributed water column contributes deep mixing — process 1-D models otherwise struggle represent. Flexible inflows — inflows can placed fixed depth (“manual” mode) allowed plunge stratify according density (“density-driven” mode), entraining ambient water sink reaching neutral buoyancy. Ice/snow model — 3-layer ice model (black ice, white ice, snow) based MyLake, depth-varying light penetration. Coupling AED2 — version 3.0 onwards, Simstrat always includes coupling AED2 biogeochemical library (coupling can switched purely physical simulations). Source code: :github: https://github.com/Eawag-AppliedSystemAnalysis/Simstrat

title: Simstrat-AED2: The 1-D k-epsilon lake model coupled with AED2
text: Diagnostics fall interpretable categories. Units descriptions taken directly AED2 source (aed2_oxygen.F90, aed2_carbon.F90, aed2_nitrogen.F90, aed2_phosphorus.F90, aed2_silica.F90, aed2_organic_matter.F90, aed2_phytoplankton.F90): Interface exchange fluxes — mass crossing atmosphere-water sediment-water interface. Verified source (aed2_oxygen.F90’s aed2_calculate_surface_oxygen/aed2_calculate_benthic_oxygen): positive means flux water column (source pelagic), negative means water column (sink), consistently interface types. Internal reaction rates — volumetric transformation rates within water column (mmol/m3/d); always non-negative (rate zero simply means process isn’t occurring, e.g. oxygen nitrification): Water-column state diagnostics — derived quantities describing current state, fluxes: Phytoplankton production nutrient uptake — aed2_phytoplankton, computed whenever module active: additional per-group diagnostics (_fI, _fNit, _fPho, _fSil, _fT, _fSal limitation factors 0-1, PPR/NPR production ratios, PAR) organic-matter photolysis rate gated behind extra_diag = true switch aed2.nml (false bundled template, since roughly double number output variables detail users won’t need day--day).

text: PHY_tchla plots plot_output() already var_aeme entry AEME’s key_naming catalog, mapped Simstrat-AED2’s PHY_TCHLA. diagnostics tabulated (PHY_GPP, OXY_atm_oxy_flux, OXY_sat, …) var_aeme entry yet — AEME hasn’t adopted every AED2 diagnostic standardised variable catalog. plot_output()/assess_aeme() recognise var_aeme names, passing unregistered one can silently resolve wrong variable via guess_aeme_vars()’s fuzzy keyword matching rather failing loudly ("PHY_GPP", instance, fuzzy-matches "PHY_green" — phytoplankton group’s biomass, gross primary production — since neither name registered). diagnostics get var_aeme entries, read straight output.nc instead: Near-surface gross primary production atmospheric oxygen exchange flux. sustained positive OXY_atm_oxy_flux indicates lake surface undersaturated drawing oxygen atmosphere (e.g. following period high respiration low photosynthesis); sustained negative flux indicates supersaturation venting oxygen atmosphere (typically strong phytoplankton bloom). code: aeme <- set_output_time_step(aeme, "hourly", daily_mean = TRUE) library(AEME)  aeme <- readRDS(system.file("extdata/aeme.rds", package = "AEME")) aeme <- set_time(aeme, start = "2020-09-01", stop = "2021-09-01",                  time_step = 3600) aeme <- set_output_time_step(aeme, "hourly", daily_mean = TRUE)  path <- file.path(tempdir(), "subdaily-demo") dir.create(path, showWarnings = FALSE) aeme <- build_aeme(path = path, aeme = aeme,                    model = c("glm_aed", "simstrat_aed2"),                    model_controls = get_model_controls(),                    ext_elev = 3, use_bgc = FALSE) aeme <- run_aeme(aeme, model = c("glm_aed", "simstrat_aed2"), path = path)  ld <- AEME:::get_lake_dir(aeme, path) for (m in c("glm_aed", "simstrat_aed2")) {   od <- file.path(ld, m, "output")   raw   <- file.size(file.path(od, "output.nc")) / 1e6   daily <- file.size(file.path(od, "output_daily.nc")) / 1e6   cat(sprintf("%-14s output.nc %6.1f MB   output_daily.nc %5.2f MB   (%.0fx)\n",               m, raw, daily, raw / daily)) } #> glm_aed        output.nc  278.3 MB   output_daily.nc  1.04 MB   (268x) #> simstrat_aed2  output.nc    9.2 MB   output_daily.nc  0.13 MB   (73x)  # get_var() returns the daily means, keyed by Date tmp <- get_var(aeme, "HYD_temp", model = "glm_aed") cat("HYD_temp Date class:", class(tmp$Date), " — days:",     length(unique(tmp$Date)), "\n") #> HYD_temp Date class: Date  — days: 365

Autocorrelation continuous series distinguish "group wins every year" "bloom happened calendar schedule system transitioning two states." match_rate/regime_shift construction works directly group wins instead, used extended index needs work. index tell whether timing right (diatom blooming spring vs. diatom blooming autumn) – plausible-looking, periodic, multi-group pattern exists . title: GLM sediment-temperature parameters from observed temperature profiles — calc_sed_temp
text: aeme Aeme object; supplied, obs_temp hypsograph extracted unless passed explicitly. Default NULL. obs_temp long df: Date, var_aeme, depth, value (degC), depths m surface. Optional aeme given. hypsograph df depth (m, +) elev, area (m2), used area-weight within zone (sed_zones = NULL) derive zones. Optional aeme given. NULL -> uniform weighting sed_zones / max_depth must supplied. sed_zones numeric vector zone upper-boundary heights bed, ascending - exactly passed GLM zone_heights. Zone 1 0 -> sed_zones[1] (deepest slab); last value may exceed max depth. NULL (default) -> estimate_sed_zones() hypsograph. max_depth max lake depth (m). NULL -> hypsograph, else deepest obs (warns). temp_var value var_aeme keep. nml_file character; name GLM nml file parameters belong , used file column parameter table. Default "glm4.nml". output one "parameters" (default) - long AEME model-parameter table param_colnames()(incl_opt = FALSE) order, ready calibration; "nml" - named list three per-zone vectors splice glm_nml[["sediment"]]; "summary" - per-zone diagnostic data.frame parameters / nml / zone_series attributes. depth_grid within-zone integration step (m). depth_tol cast used zone deepest sample within depth_tol m top zone's depth band. min_obs, min_months thresholds harmonic fit (else monthly-range). default_mean, default_amplitude, default_peak_doy last-resort values. default_peak_doy = 46 mid-Feb (S. hemisphere summer); use ~209 N. borrow_amp_factor, borrow_lag_days unfitted deep zone borrows cycle nearest shallower fitted zone: damp amplitude borrow_amp_factor^(zone steps) lag peak_doy borrow_lag_days per step. verbose logical; print assembled per-zone table, nml snippet parameter table.

title: GLM sediment-temperature parameters from observed temperature profiles — calc_sed_temp
text: Depends output: "parameters" - data.frame columns model, file, name, value, min, max, group, index; one row per zone sediment/sed_temp_mean, sediment/sed_temp_amplitude sediment/sed_temp_peak_doy. "nml" - named list sed_temp_mean / sed_temp_amplitude / sed_temp_peak_doy, per-zone numeric vector GLM zone order. "summary" - per-zone diagnostic data.frame (zone 1 = deepest), carrying "parameters" table, ready--paste "nml" snippet per-zone "zone_series" attributes.

Flagged outside [1, 36525] (1 day 100 years) – lake flushing day, essentially never, usually indicates units magnitude problem rather real lake. hydraulic_loading_m_yr: annual discharge divided lake surface area, metres water per year. Flagged outside [0.01, 1e5] m/yr. implied_conc_*: flow-weighted mean concentration implied load / discharge NIT_amm, NIT_nit, PHS_frp, CAR_doc CHM_oxy (present), checked plausible ranges used standardise_inflow(). Thresholds deliberately loose (order--magnitude) clearly implausible values flagged.

title: Parameter library for the GLM-AED model. — glm_aed_parameter_library
text: data frame 452 rows 9 variables: module Character. configuration block (GLM) module (AED) parameter belongs . GLM modules correspond Fortran namelist blocks glm3.nml (e.g., "glm_setup", "mixing", "morphometry", "time", "output", "init_profiles", "light", "bird_model", "sediment", "snowice", "meteorology", "inflow", "outflow", "wq_setup"). AED modules correspond namelist blocks aed.nml (e.g., "aed_oxygen", "aed_nitrogen", "aed_phosphorus", "aed_silica", "aed_phytoplankton", "aed_sedflux", "aed_seddiagenesis"). group Character. optional sub-category grouping related parameters process function within module. example, "nitrification", "denitrification", "sediment_flux" within aed_nitrogen module; "radiation", "wind", "rainfall" within meteorology module. Empty string ("") sub-grouping applies. parameter Character. parameter name used configuration file (e.g., "max_layers", "Fsed_oxy", "R_nitrif"). label Character. short, human-readable label parameter (e.g., "Layers", "Sediment O2 flux", "Nitrification rate"). symbol Character. mathematical symbol used model documentation equations, rendered plain text (e.g., "N_MAX", "F_sed^oxy", "theta_nitrif"). Empty string symbol defined. description Character. description parameter, role model, relevant context. units Character. units parameter. Uses "-" dimensionless quantities, "string" text parameters, "boolean" logical switches. Physical units follow standard abbreviations (e.g., "m", "mmol O2/m3", "mmol N/m2/d", "/d"). default Character. default value parameter documented, empty string ("") default specified source documentation. source Character. URL documentation page parameter information extracted. GLM parameters sourced https://aquatic.science.uwa.edu.au/research/models/GLM/configuration.html AED parameters individual chapter pages AED Science Manual https://aquaticecodynamics.github.io/aed-science/.

title: Parameter library for the GLM-AED model. — glm_aed_parameter_library
text: Parameters organised module (namelist block AED module belong ) optionally group (sub-category describing process context, "nitrification", "sediment_flux", "radiation"). GLM (General Lake Model) parameters configure hydrodynamic model, including layer structure, mixing, morphometry, meteorological forcing, boundary conditions (inflows outflows), light penetration, ice/snow dynamics, sediment heat exchange. AED (Aquatic EcoDynamics) parameters configure water quality biogeochemical modules couple GLM. modules included dataset cover dissolved oxygen, inorganic nitrogen (ammonium, nitrate, nitrification, denitrification), inorganic phosphorus (phosphate, adsorption), silica, phytoplankton (growth, light, nutrient uptake, respiration, mortality, settling), sediment biogeochemistry (static sediment fluxes via aed_sedflux dynamic diagenesis via aed_seddiagenesis). Note aed_phytoplankton parameters listed groups "growth", "light", "nitrogen", "phosphorus", "silica" per-phytoplankton-group parameters typically specified separate phyto_data namelist file rather directly aed.nml.

Logical/character nml values (e.g. glm_setup::non_avg) vector-valued/indexed nml parameters (e.g. per sediment zone) skipped, since catalogue lake-specific notion vector's true length recovering part corrupt field written back via input_model_parameters(). returned object configuration()$calc_wbal, calc_wlev, ext_elev set FALSE/FALSE/0, rather build_aeme()'s defaults TRUE/TRUE/0. loaded inflows()/outflows()/hypsograph already reflect finished water balance lake-level calculation; leaving calc_wbal/calc_wlev build_aeme() defaults make subsequent build_aeme(aeme = ., use_aeme = TRUE) call recompute silently overwrite loaded values (use_aeme = TRUE preserves raw nml text – disable water-balance/lake-level recalculation runs per-model config files written). Passing calc_wbal/calc_wlev/ext_elev explicitly later build_aeme() call overrides stored values usual. GLM version configuration read (e.g. "glm3.nml" "glm4.nml") recorded configuration()$glm_aed$hydrodynamic_file, later write_configuration() build_aeme() call writes back filename rather assuming glm3.nml.

title: Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) fit function — kge

title: Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) fit function — kge
text: numeric; KGE, maximum 1 (perfect fit). Returns NA undefined (e.g., zero observed variance mean).

title: Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) fit function — kge
text: KGE decomposes fit three components instead conflating way nse's single squared-error term : $$\text{KGE} = 1 - \sqrt{(r - 1)^2 + (\alpha - 1)^2 + (\beta - 1)^2}$$ variability ratio (\(\alpha\)) bias ratio (\(\beta\)) calculated : $$\alpha = \frac{\sigma_{\text{sim}}}{\sigma_{\text{obs}}}, \quad \beta = \frac{\mu_{\text{sim}}}{\mu_{\text{obs}}}$$ \(r\) Pearson correlation, \(\sigma\) standard deviation, \(\mu\) mean. Maximum 1 (perfect fit). dimensionless like NSE, also reasonable choice combining fit values across variables different units magnitudes, generally preferred NSE current hydrological/environmental modelling practice. calib_aeme() run_and_fit() minimise values returned FUN_list entries - use kge_loss (returns -1 * kge(obs, sim)) calibration objective.

text: numeric; KGE', maximum 1 (perfect fit). Returns NA undefined.

title: Modified Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE') fit function — kge_prime
text: $$\text{KGE}' = 1 - \sqrt{(r - 1)^2 + (\gamma - 1)^2 + (\beta - 1)^2}$$ coefficient--variation ratio (\(\gamma\)) decouples variability term bias term cleanly: $$\gamma = \frac{\sigma_{\text{sim}} / \mu_{\text{sim}}}{\sigma_{\text{obs}} / \mu_{\text{obs}}}$$ generally recommended default original KGE. Returned conventional orientation higher better (1 = perfect fit). calib_aeme() run_and_fit() minimise values returned FUN_list entries - use kge_prime_loss (returns -1 * kge_prime(obs, sim)) calibration objective.

title: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) fit function — mae
text: $$\text{MAE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^n |\text{sim}_i - \text{obs}_i|$$ Already 0 (perfect fit) best increasing fit worsens, minimise-oriented -needs _loss companion - pass straight FUN_list, calib_aeme run_and_fit minimise. MAE stays variable's native units, directly comparable across variables different units magnitudes - summing MAE , say, temperature fit (degC) oxygen fit (mg/L) multi-variable FUN_list lets whichever variable happens larger natural magnitude dominate combined fit. Prefer dimensionless metric nse_loss kge_loss combining fits across variables; MAE/RMSE suited single-variable calibration reporting fit interpretable, original units.

title: Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) fit function — nse
text: NSE calculated : $$\text{NSE} = 1 - \frac{\sum_{=1}^n (\text{obs}_i - \text{sim}_i)^2}{\sum_{=1}^n (\text{obs}_i - \bar{\text{obs}})^2}$$ ranges -Inf 1 (1 = perfect fit, 0 = better mean observations). dimensionless, makes reasonable default combining fit values across variables different units magnitudes - squared-error based, -weights peaks -weights errors low/baseline range, conflates bias, variability timing error one number. See kge/kge_prime fit function keeps separate. calib_aeme() run_and_fit() minimise values returned FUN_list entries, nse() suitable calibration objective directly - use nse_loss (returns -1 * nse(obs, sim)) .

title: Percent Bias (PBIAS) fit function — pbias
text: Calculates absolute percent bias observed modelled values - average tendency modelled values larger (positive bias) smaller (negative bias) observed values, expressed percentage observed total:

title: Percent Bias (PBIAS) fit function — pbias
code: pbias(obs, sim, na.rm = TRUE)

title: Percent Bias (PBIAS) fit function — pbias
text: obs Numeric vector observed values. sim Numeric vector simulated (modelled) values. na.rm Logical; missing values (NA) either vector removed pairwise computation? Default TRUE.

title: Percent Bias (PBIAS) fit function — pbias
text: numeric; absolute percent bias. Returns NA sum obs zero.

title: Percent Bias (PBIAS) fit function — pbias
text: $$\text{PBIAS} = 100 \times \left| \frac{\sum_{=1}^n (\text{sim}_i - \text{obs}_i)}{\sum_{=1}^n \text{obs}_i} \right|$$ Already 0 (perfect fit, systematic bias) best increasing fit worsens either direction, minimise-oriented -needs _loss companion - pass straight FUN_list, calib_aeme run_and_fit minimise. absolute value used rather signed value, since equally large - -estimate equally poor fit - minimising signed value instead push calibration towards negative (-estimating) bias possible. Unlike mae/rmse, expressed percentage observed total rather variable's native units, makes directly comparable across variables different units magnitudes - similar nse/kge respect. captures systematic /-estimation, timing, variability shape - typically combined NSE KGE (largely insensitive consistent bias) rather used alone. See Moriasi et al. (2007) commonly used PBIAS performance thresholds.

title: Plot model performance metrics — plot_assess
text: Visualise model performance statistics returned assess_aeme. Four complementary views available via type: "dot" - Cleveland dot plot, one facet per metric free x-axis, points coloured model. general-purpose default: keeps metrics scales native-unit errors (bias, rmse, nmae) bounded skill scores (nse, kge, d2, r) forced onto common axis. "heatmap" - Tile plot model (x) variable (y), faceted metric. Fill value rescaled 0-1 within metric/variable oriented 1 best-performing model; raw value printed tile. "taylor" - Normalised Taylor diagram (Taylor, 2001), one point per model per variable, encoding correlation ratio modelled observed standard deviation. observations plot (1, 0). "target" - Target diagram (Jolliff et al., 2009), plotting normalised bias normalised unbiased RMSD. Points inside unit circle total RMSD smaller observed standard deviation.

text: $$\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^n (\text{sim}_i - \text{obs}_i)^2}$$ Already 0 (perfect fit) best increasing fit worsens, minimise-oriented -needs _loss companion pass straight FUN_list, calib_aeme run_and_fit minimise. Like mae, RMSE stays variable's native units directly comparable across variables different units magnitudes combined multi-variable FUN_list - see mae details. what: Run a single what-if model scenario from a path alone — run_model_test
title: Run a single what-if model scenario from a path alone — run_model_test
text: Generic driver quickly testing different parameters, nml/yaml/par settings, inflow/outflow concentrations, initial conditions existing GLM-AED, GOTM-WET, Simstrat-AED Simstrat-AED2 configuration directory, without needing aeme object. Dispatches model's thin path-based wrapper functions (e.g. set_glm_param()/ set_glm_init()/set_glm_inflows()/set_glm_outflows()/ run_glm_aed()/read_glm_output() model = "glm_aed") scenario code can written pointed supported model.

title: Run a single what-if model scenario from a path alone — run_model_test
code: run_model_test(   model,   path,   param_overrides = list(),   init = list(),   inflow_args = NULL,   outflow_args = NULL,   tgt_vars = NULL,   verbose = FALSE,   safe = TRUE )

title: Run a single what-if model scenario from a path alone — run_model_test
text: model character; one "glm_aed", "gotm_wet", "simstrat_aed", "simstrat_aed2". path filepath; directory containing existing model configuration edit run (already written build_aeme()). param_overrides named list parameter/value pairs, forwarded model's set_*_param() wrapper, e.g. list(Kw = 0.5) GLM-AED list(`time.dt` = 1800) GOTM-WET. Empty list (default) leaves parameters unchanged. init named list forwarded model's set_*_init() wrapper, e.g. list(temp = seq(20, 10, length.= 10), wq_init = list(NIT_amm = 0.5)). Empty list (default) leaves initial conditions unchanged. inflow_args named list forwarded model's set_*_inflows() wrapper; must include data, named list inflow data.frames (see add_inflow()). NULL (default) leaves inflows unchanged. outflow_args named list forwarded model's set_*_outflows() wrapper; must include data, named list outflow data.frames (see add_outflows()), plus arguments model requires (e.g. heights_wdr, surface_elev Simstrat). NULL (default) leaves outflows unchanged. tgt_vars character vector output variables read back (passed vars_sim model's read_*_output() wrapper, also used decide derived variables – e.g. "HYD_thmcln" – compute via add_deriv_output()). NULL (default) reads every variable reader returns default, adds derived variables – request explicitly name get . verbose logical; passed model's run_*() wrapper. safe logical; TRUE (default), failed edit model run caught reported message() instead stopping – useful looping many scenarios one bad combination abort rest. Set FALSE let errors propagate normally.

title: Run a single what-if model scenario from a path alone — run_model_test
text: list requested output variables (returned model's read_*_output() wrapper, derived variables added via add_deriv_output()), NULL safe = TRUE edit/run/read failed.

text: *_args list applied via .call() corresponding thin wrapper, path supplied automatically first argument – names inside list must match wrapper's arguments. inflow_args/outflow_args exception: data.frame list argument always named data (regardless underlying wrapper's naming – list_inf/inf_list/inf), extra arguments underlying outflow writer requires (e.g. Simstrat's heights_wdr/ surface_elev) passed alongside name.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ run_model_test("glm_aed", path_glm, param_overrides = list(Kw = 0.8),                tgt_vars = "HYD_temp") run_model_test("simstrat_aed2", path_simstrat,                init = list(wq_init = list(NIT_amm = 0.5)),                tgt_vars = "HYD_temp") } # }

Recognised columns (optional except noted): name outlet label, used messages. type GLM outlet_type: 1 fixed, 2 floating, 3 adaptive/target-temperature, 4-5 withdrawal modes, 6 submerged. Default 2. float logical flt_off_sw. Default type == 2. GLM forces floating outlet type = 2. elev outlet elevation (m, hypsography datum) - see Outlet elevation convention. Required every outlet unless existing block already outl_elvs entry . bsn_len, bsn_wid basin length / width outlet (m). Computed hypsography omitted. factor outflow_factor, per-outlet flow multiplier. Default 1. file outflow_fl, path outlet's flow-forcing CSV, relative path_glm. Carried existing block omitted outlet count unchanged. target_temp target_temp (degC) type == 3. crit outlet_crit, per-outlet critical threshold (Hcrit). subm_elev subm_elev_outflow type == 6: fixed submerged elevation height bed (m), 0 <= subm_elev <= max depth. elev_idx elev_idx_outflow type == 6: dynamic layer index overrides subm_elev. Use NA / -1 none. surface_elev current lake surface elevation (m, hypsography datum), used convert floating outlet's elev depth surface. Default: min(H) + lake_depth read nml. seepage, seepage_rate enable constant bed seepage set rate (m/day). NULL leaves current value. withdr_temp_file withdrTemp_fl: single target-withdrawal- temperature forcing CSV (relative path_glm) shared adaptive outlets. NULL leaves current value; NA removes . adaptive named list block-level adaptive-withdrawal controls, crit_val, crit_dep, crit_days, crit_above, crit_varname, crit_idx, min_lake_temp, fac_range_upper, fac_range_lower, mix_withdraw, coupl_oxy_sw. supplied names written. crest_width, crest_factor weir / overflow geometry surface outlet. NULL leaves current value. thick_limit outflow_thick_limit: minimum layer thickness (m) outlet draw . NULL leaves current value. single_layer_draw logical single_layer_draw: force outlet draw single layer elevation. NULL leaves current value. extra named list raw &outflow keys set verbatim (e.g. time_fmt, timezone). Applied last, overrides . bathy data.frame elev / area columns (hypsograph), used size outlets validate elevations. Default: H / arrays nml's &morphometry block. dims_lake length-2 numeric c(basin_length, basin_width) crest. Default: nml's bsn_len / bsn_wid. validate check every value GLM's ranges writing abort violation. Default TRUE. glm_file path GLM nml. Default: discovered path_glm.

title: Write model configuration from the aeme object — write_configuration
text: Writes requested model's configuration files straight aeme object's cached state, recomputation kind – hydrodynamic/bgc files come verbatim configuration(aeme), (include_boundary = TRUE) meteorology/inflow/outflow boundary-condition files come straight input(aeme)/inflows(aeme)/ outflows(aeme), bypassing build_aeme()'s water-balance/lake-level/ AED-re-derivation pipeline entirely. makes safe choice rewriting already-built (glm_config_to_aeme()-loaded) configuration disk unchanged – e.g. fresh directory – without risk build_aeme(use_aeme = TRUE) silently regenerating values generic state instead trusting cached.

title: Write model configuration from the aeme object — write_configuration
text: aeme Aeme object. model character vector; models use. One "dy_cd", "glm_aed", "gotm_wet", "simstrat_aed2". Defaults models found aeme. path character; path directory model configuration written. Default current working directory. include_boundary logical; also write model's boundary-condition files (meteorology, inflows outflows, e.g. GLM-AED's bcs/meteo_glm.csv, bcs/inflow_*.csv bcs/outflow_*.csv) model's format, straight input(aeme)/inflows(aeme)/ outflows(aeme). Default TRUE. apply_params logical; apply parameters(aeme) writing. configuration-file parameters set configuration written, (boundary files) met/inflow/outflow scaling parameters applied data written. Neither configuration(aeme) input(aeme)/inflows(aeme)/outflows(aeme) changed: parameters affect reaches disk. Parameters file configuration (e.g. bgc parameters model built without bgc) skipped warning. Default TRUE.

title: Consolidate Simstrat-AED2/AED text output into a single netCDF file — write_simstrat_nc
text: AED's sediment-zone output (Simstrat-AED , AED2) written second, separate family files, <var>_zone_out.dat – one column per benthic zone (labelled zone's reference depth), alongside regular <var>_out.dat variable (single lake-bottom whole-lake value). exist side side variable name _zone_out.dat ends _out.dat, share water-column z dimension/grid way regular depth-profile variables – silently wrote zone values wrong depths (failed outright column-count mismatch) whenever zone file's column count happen match shared z grid's length. get zone netCDF dimension instead, coordinate-valued zone's reference depth (m). Variable names keep _zone suffix (stripping trailing _out.dat, every file), e.g. NIT_amm_dsf_out.dat NIT_amm_dsf_zone_out.dat become distinct netCDF variables NIT_amm_dsf (dims time) NIT_amm_dsf_zone (dims zone, time) – never colliding. Reading back needs extra code: read_simstrat_output's load_all sweep already routes variable whose dimensions (time) (z, time) .read_glm_grouped_var new_grouped_var object, generic path GLM-AED's nzones-dimensioned output uses.

what: Phytoplankton default fixes and a new succession-diagnostic function
title: AEME 0.4.0
text: Follow-investigation whether GLM-AED can reproduce genuine multi-group phytoplankton succession (diatom/green/cyanobacteria), surfaced two structural issues shipped aed_phyto_pars.csv template (inst/extdata/aed/aed_phyto_pars.csv) affect every lake built package defaults, just one investigated: X_nmin/X_nmax/X_pmin/X_pmax (Droop internal-quota bounds) byte-identical across every phytoplankton group. template’s configuration (simINDynamics/simIPDynamics = 2 every group), bounds – K_N/K_P, apply rare edge case – actual nutrient-competition lever, shipping identical meant group-level nutrient differentiation possible regardless else tuned. Given modest, literature-informed, stability-tested differentiation: cyanobacteria get wider phosphorus luxury-storage range (X_pmin 0.001->0.0007, X_pmax 0.005->0.009, reflecting documented polyphosphate storage bloom-forming taxa), diatoms get tighter, efficient nitrogen/phosphorus economy (X_nmin 0.02->0.025, X_nmax 0.07->0.055, X_pmin 0.001->0.0012, X_pmax 0.005->0.0038, reflecting documented low-luxury nutrient uptake diatoms relative greens/ cyanobacteria). Every group unchanged. simSiUptake 0 () every group, including diatom. Per aed_phyto_pars.csv’s dbase aed_bio_utils.F90’s phyto_fSi(), switch gates whether silica limitation computed – fSi defaults 1 (unlimited) whenever ’s . diatom group structurally requires silica; shipping default switch meant silica limitation silently inert one group ’s supposed apply . Now 1 diatom, unchanged (0) every group. (third candidate fix – aed_zooplankton absent lake’s active &aed_models list, silently zeroes top-grazing – turned already correct package’s default inst/extdata/aed/aed.nml; omission found investigation specific one external project’s lake configuration, package default.)

title: AEME 0.4.0
text: New exported function computing system-level diagnostic whether model run shows genuine, recurring, multi-group phytoplankton succession – computed purely model output via get_var(), observations required. Returns three components (evenness, dom_entropy, periodicity) plus composite; see ?aed_succession_index one catches two failed designs (raw autocorrelation; naive mode-matching) led current match_rate/regime_shift construction periodicity. Intended PEST regularisation observation (biasing calibration away single-group-monopoly one-way-drift solutions) standalone diagnostic.

title: AEME 0.4.0
text: GLM-AED outflow setup wrote nonsensical outl_elvs coerced bsn_len_outl / bsn_wid_outl NA lakes whose hypsography extends 0 m, e.g. lake bed sea level. Several problems build_glm(), rooted -1 AEME’s “specified” sentinel outflow elevation (add_outflows(); build_aeme() sets water-balance outflow -1): sentinel recognised via heights_wdr <= 0, lake bed 0 m real request swallowed, -1 sentinel leak literal elevation; “specified” replacement init_depth - 1, water depth written outl_elvs, fixed outlet GLM reads absolute elevation hypsography datum - fell outside hypsography elipse_dims()’s area lookup returned NA; outlet_type / flt_off_sw inferred sign elevation (ifelse(heights_wdr < 0, 2, 1)), default -1 sentinel silently produced floating offtake, GLM expects outl_elvs depth surface [0, depth] rejects negative values (“lake surface”). build_glm() now interprets outflow elevation explicitly: -1 / NA sentinel means specified defaults floating offtake (outlet_type = 2, flt_off_sw = .true.) drawing ~1 m bed tracking surface, outl_elvs written depth--surface GLM requires floating outlet; explicit elevation placed fixed outlet absolute elevation, validated clamped [base_elev, crest_elev]. Basin length/width looked outlet’s true absolute elevation (make_wdr_glm() gained dims_elev argument ) clamped range(bathy$elev) set_glm_outflows() call --range outlet still yields finite dimensions. lakes whose hypsography sits /0 m generated &outflow block unchanged; sub-sea-level lakes previously failed now build. set_glm_outflow_config() (new, exported) — fine-grained control GLM-AED &outflow block existing configuration, beyond fixed/floating split set_glm_outflows() offers: per-outlet adaptive/target-temperature (type 3) submerged (type 6) outlets, outlet_crit thresholds, target_temp, withdrTemp_fl, bed seepage / seepage_rate, weir crest_width / crest_factor, outflow_thick_limit single_layer_draw, plus adaptive list block-level crit_* controls. Elevations given hypsography datum converted per outlet; every value checked GLM’s ranges (src/glm_init.c) writing. edits nml, leaving flow-forcing CSVs alone. run_aeme() reported successful run failed opaque netCDF error (open_nc_safe(): “File path must single character string”) model crashed. Three causes: GLM-AED built gfortran, whose STOP "..." (e.g. malformed aed_noncohesive namelist) exits 0, run_aeme()’s status == 0 success test passed; verbose = TRUE path run_glm_aed()/run_gotm_wet() checked nothing , leaving misleading cli tick; failed model still handed load_output(). Now run_*() attaches logical $success (exit status model’s completion banner, Simstrat netCDF conversion), run_aeme() gates “Model run complete!” message output loading , read_model_outputs() aborts clear aeme_error_missing_output (“re-run verbose = TRUE”) expected output file absent. cli_inform_safe() cli_safe() forward evaluation environment cli, message containing {} expression referenced local variable calling function failed object '<name>' found — cli interpolating wrapper’s frame. surfaced building Aeme object whose inflow tables still used pre-standard column names (e.g. NIT_din), standardise_inflow() reports "Renaming {length(matched)} column{?s}". wrappers now take .envir = parent.frame() pass . read_model_config() assumed .par configuration file Simstrat’s JSON format, DYRESM-CAEDYM’s dyresm3p1.par shares extension plain text - read_model_config(model = "dy_cd", ...) failed lake DYRESM-CAEDYM configuration. Now scoped model == "simstrat_aed2" . Fixed lake-level inversion bug affecting every Simstrat-AED2 simulation non-trivial inflows/outflows: .write_simstrat_grid_file() wrote two-point depth header used force non-zero trapezoidal integration descending order, Simstrat’s Integrate() computes dx = x() - x(-1) directly file’s (unreordered) depth values. descending header therefore silently negated every flux writer produces - inflow, outflow, temperature, salinity, AED2 inflow concentrations alike - simulated lake level Simstrat-AED2 tracked opposite direction three models. Fixed writing depths ascending order; verified comparing Simstrat’s Qvert output variable expected net inflow/outflow signal (now matching almost exactly, correlation 0.9986, vs. exact sign-flip fix). calc_evap() gained dedicated model == "simstrat_aed2" branch implementing Simstrat’s evaporation formula (Livingstone & Imboden wind function Gill (1992) saturation vapour pressure, strat_forcing.f90), used estimate_lake_wlev() fitting water balance Simstrat-AED2. previously shared GLM-AED’s simpler bulk-aerodynamic formula. build_aeme() call migrate_aeme(), Aeme object saved simstrat_aed2 existed (missing time$spin_up[["simstrat_aed2"]]) crash inside check_time()’s compute_spinup_dates() first time built newer AEME version. build_aeme() now migrates object entry, matching check_aeme()/show()/plot(). write_simstrat_nc() mishandled AED’s sediment-zone output (<var>_zone_out.dat, Simstrat-AED ). files also match general *_out.dat glob written shared water-column z dimension/grid used regular depth-profile variables, either put zone values wrong depths failed outright whenever zone file’s column count (one per benthic zone) didn’t happen match water column’s level count. Zone variables now get zone netCDF dimension, coordinate-valued zone’s reference depth keeping existing <var> new <var>_zone variables distinct. changes needed reading side: read_simstrat_output()’s load_all sweep already routes variable shaped (time) (z, time) generic grouped-variable path GLM-AED’s nzones-dimensioned output uses, zone variables come back aeme_grouped_var objects automatically. Verified real Simstrat-AED Rotorua run (75 sediment-zone variables across 3 zones).
